title: Steady-state kernel anchoring — weekly standup notes
body:
Context:
Quick sync from the steady-state kernel anchoring working group — aim is to stabilize kernel handoff behavior under steady arrival rates and avoid oscillations in batch composition when KV cache hit-rates change. This doc captures weekend experiments, standup highlights, and next steps (rough notes).

Attendees:
- Lena (owner)
- Marco, Priya, Samir, Ruth 
- Dropped in: Tina (SRE), CJ (benchmarks)

High-level summary (tl;dr):
- New anchoring heuristic (anchor-on-prefill-score) reduced p95 dispatch jitter by ~18% in canary across 8x A100 pool; throughput unchanged; small increase (~0.8%) in median latency for 4-token prompts — acceptable trade for stability.
- KV-cache compaction schedule prototype prevented a cascade eviction scenario during the synthetic shadow workload run; still seeing short-term miss spikes at hour boundaries.
- Micro-batch splitter patch (PR 489) ready for merge after one more perf run; it fixes a pathological case where small chat sessions were repeatedly split and increased tail latency.

Notes and experiment results (raw):
1) Anchoring heuristic test (branch: anchoring/steady-jan):
- Setup: steady 650 qps simulated; mix: 60% chat (avg 48 tokens), 40% short-completion (avg 12 tokens).
- Metric: dispatch jitter = stddev(inter-dispatch-interval) across kernels.
- Before: jitter 7.6ms; After: jitter 6.2ms (–18%).
- Observed: slightly higher micro-queueing at kernel accept stage when cache-hit drift > 6%. Hypothesis: anchors delay rebalancing until prefetch signals are stable.
- TODO: add a fast-exit path for anchors when queue depth > 150 to avoid backpressure. (Owner: Marco, JIRA-SRV-1412-comment)

2) KV-cache compaction schedule (proto):
- Implemented time-aligned compaction windows (10m sliding, staggered per-shard) to avoid simultaneous TTL sweeps.
- Result: under synthetic spike (2x baseline for 3m), evictions aligned and downstream cache miss rate spike reduced from 9.8% -> 3.1%.
- Remaining issue: boundary spike at compaction window rollover (00:10 relative to shard start).
- Quick mitigation: jitter window offset per-shard (configurable) — Priya to roll out A/B to 10% of traffic.

3) Micro-batch splitter (PR 489):
- Fix: avoids repeated split/merge oscillation when token-length distribution is bimodal.
- Bench: reduced token-cost for small-chat cohort by 12% in the lab; tail latency down 5–7% under modest load.
- Risk: introduces slight CPU overhead in scheduler (measured +3% at peak).
- Plan: merge after smoke test on next canary (Ruth).

Operational notes / incidents:
- Friday 02:10 PST: short spike in cache misses correlated with compaction window alignment; SRE paged on-call. Root cause traced to uncoordinated compaction across 12 shards. Resolved by temporary rolling pause on compaction.
- Nightwatch: prefilling agent crashed once (OOM) on shard-17 during heavy shadowing. Crash dump in linked_artifacts. Samir to open follow-up.

Risks & open questions:
- Does anchoring create long-lived allocation of KV lines for low-volume customers? Need guardrails to avoid fairness regressions. Action: add customer-level TTL cutoff in anchoring (Lena/Macro).
- Compaction window jitter tradeoff: how wide before compaction inefficiencies harm hit-rate? Priya to run a sweep (0–60s jitter) and report.
- Micro-batch splitter CPU overhead: does it interact badly with GPU power-savings governor? Ask infra team to validate. (Ticket: JIRA-SRV-1429)

Action items (short):
- Marco: implement fast-exit path for anchors when queue depth high (estimate 2d) — track in JIRA-SRV-1412.
- Priya: rollout staggered compaction jitter A/B (10% traffic) and collect 48h metrics (start 2026-01-13).
- Ruth: smoke canary for PR 489 on 2026-01-14; post results in slack thread.
- Samir: investigate prefilling agent OOM, attach heap profile + cgroup settings (JIRA-SRV-1421).
- Lena: draft short playbook paragraph describing steady-state anchoring behavior for oncall responders (due 2026-01-16).

Notes-to-self / scratchpad (less formal):
- Consider keeping a 30s rolling average of cache-hit by customer to feed anchoring decisions — might smooth weirdness for low qps clients.
- If we add anchor fast-exit, watch for thrash where anchors flip on and off at medium queue depths. Might need hysteresis.
- Slack refs: ops-kernel-anchoring #6789 has raw flame graphs and the crash dump link.

Meeting cadence proposal (sync):
- Keep weekly deep-dive on Tuesdays 11:00 PT for experiments and Friday 09:30 PT short triage for incidents.
- Temporary daily 15m standup next week while compaction A/B is running.

Appendix (quick links):
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://perf.redwood/serve/anchoring/canary
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/489
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRV-1412

End of notes.

Draft status: rough; this is a working doc — please leave inline comments.
